research_notes: The "EVE Energy Yancheng plant" is the SKOJ joint-venture cell plant in Yancheng, Jiangsu, China. It was a JV in which SK On held 70% and China's EVE Energy (EVE Power) held 30%. plant_name: Lishen Mianyang Southwest Production Base
research_notes:

Capacity: sourced figures are given in Ah, not GWh. ~300 million Ah/yr of cells per phase converts to roughly ~1 GWh/yr per phase at LFP-range cell voltage (300M Ah x ~3.2 V ≈ 0.96 GWh), i.e. an eventual cell nameplate of perhaps ~1-2 GWh/yr if both cell phases were built. Because the GWh conversion relies on an unsourced voltage assumption and Phase 3 completion is unconfirmed, nameplate_capacity_gwh is left null rather than guessed. This is a comparatively small, older base, not one of Lishen's flagship multi-GWh sites.

Chemistry: sources describe "power lithium battery" for NEVs but do not specify LFP vs NMC for Mianyang, so chemistry left null. End market recorded as EV (power/pack for new-energy vehicles). Coordinates left null (Hebei-Pingwu industrial park within Mianyang High-Tech Zone; precise plant coordinates not confirmed).

Caution: an unverified search summary claimed a separate "18 GWh LFP, RMB 10bn, signed May 2022" Mianyang project, but this could NOT be corroborated and appears to conflate other Lishen bases (Wuxi 24 GWh/RMB 11.2bn; Chuzhou 36 GWh/RMB 15.2bn) or the unrelated Chuangming/Creative New Energy Mianyang project.
